title: Add response-format UX hints and stream-safe toolcall fencing
author: Asha Reddy
description: Summary: Add a lightweight "validation_hint" metadata layer to response_format validation failures and a stream-safe toolcall fencing mechanism. Motivation: strict mode currently returns a hard rejection on first schema violation during streaming, which forces clients to restart interactions and makes tool/function-call invocations brittle. This PR introduces an opt-in route-level 'strictness_suggest' mode that returns actionable repair hints during validation failures and defers final hard-rejection until a stream checkpoint. It also prevents partial tool/function calls from being emitted when the validator detects unrecoverable semantics at the tool-call boundary, ensuring downstream systems do not perform side-effecting operations on malformed payloads. Changes: - response_format: introduce validation_hint field in validation failures with structured short messages and a single-line suggested_fix text (machine-friendly; clients can present to users or auto-rewrite prompts). - API surface: add response_format.strictness_mode with options [off, suggest, strict]; default remains off for backwards compatibility. - Streaming: add stream checkpoint points (stream_snapshot tokens) where the runtime will evaluate accumulated output against the schema and either emit a hint (suggest mode) or close the stream with a deterministic error (strict mode). - Tool/function calling: implement a fencing check performed before committing a tool call; if the validator indicates the current token buffer is uncertain, the call is withheld and a diagnostic hint is emitted instead. If the downstream receives the fencing signal, SDKs will retry after client-provided fixes. - OpenAI compatibility: adapt shim layer so that function_call objects are only forwarded when the fence is clear; in suggest mode we synthesize a 'function_call_suggestion' wrapper instead of a direct call. - Observability: add metrics (schema.hints_emitted, schema.fence_blocks, schema.checkpoint_latency) and tracing tags to correlate hints with eval prompt IDs. - Docs & SDK: add JS + Python SDK helpers to surface validation_hint and a short example snippet that rewrites the prompt automatically when a suggestion is present. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged (off). The new fields are opt-in at route level and also gated by API version. Tests: unit + e2e tests added, including simulated streaming sessions that exercise partial JSON emission and ensure fences prevent tool calls. Rollout plan: feature-flag behind FF-schema-hints; gradual rollout to internal customers; monitor schema.fence_blocks and client-side adoption. Links: Linear ENG-1482 (design doc), internal RFC (rfc/2026-schema-hints.md). Checklist: - [x] API contract and proto updates - [x] Runtime streaming checkpoints - [x] Toolcall fencing logic - [x] SDK surface + examples - [x] Unit/e2e tests - [x] Metrics/tracing - [x] Docs update

feat(runtime): checkpointing and stream_snapshot token support
fix(openai-compat): wrap function_call suggestions behind fence
chore(sdk): expose validation hint helpers in js+py

review_comments: Miguel Ortega: Nice approach. Two concerns: 1) can we make the hint payload strictly small to avoid adding token overhead to the stream? 2) how will the fence interact with retries on idempotent tool calls?

Author (Asha): Good points. Hints are capped to 256 bytes and we add a header-free compressed form for internal telemetry. Fencing is conservative: idempotent tool calls include an allowlist and we record fence reasons so SDKs can auto-retry after client fix.
Priya Sharma: Please add an integration test that simulates an early partial JSON that would have invoked a tool call if not fenced (I see tests added, but be explicit).
Author (Asha): Added explicit e2e scenario 'partial-tool-call-fence' as requested.
Evan Liu: Approving after minor nits on naming (use function_call_suggestion instead of suggested_function_call to be clearer).
Author (Asha): Renamed variable and updated docs as requested. Thanks!
release_notes: Introduce an opt-in response_format.strictness_mode with a 'suggest' mode that emits small machine-friendly validation_hint messages during streaming and a stream-safe fencing mechanism that prevents partial tool/function calls when schema validation is uncertain. Backwards compatible; feature-flagged behind FF-schema-hints.
